newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU stats group to meet on France-Telecom.
newsitem.headline: EU stats group to meet on France-Telecom.

text.p: The European Union advisory group on financial statistics is to meet on Monday evening at the Bundesbank in Frankfurt to discuss pension payments from France-Telecom and France's public deficit, a European Commission spokesman said.

He said that there was no possibility of a change in the Commission's view that such payments from France-Telecom can be included in calculations on whether France meets the convergence criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). "The decision is taken," he said.
The European Commission said last week that EUROSTAT, its statistical arm, had ruled that France-Telecom receipts were acceptable in gauging France's EMU standing.

Previously, various advisory groups had failed to reach agreement on the issue. The committee meeting in Frankfurt on Monday was one of those groups advising the Commission, the spokesman said. He denied reports that EUROSTAT had rushed to a decision without receiving the input requested by the advisory group from all EU member states.
"It was not a pre-condition for the EUROSTAT decision that all contributions would be received," he said.
The spokesman reiterated that the group could not change the decision that had already been made.

The French government has proposed transferring 37.5 billion francs from France Telecom as a vital element in cutting its 1997 budget deficit to three percent of GDP, the target for EU nations seeking membership of the European single currency.
The payment would be in exchange for the government assuming the state-owned telephone operator's pension liabilities.

Critics have said the one-off transfer smacked of creative accounting and ran counter to Maastricht Treaty guidelines for countries to take sustainable economic measures to qualify for the planned 1999 start of the single currency.
